svg.title: Digital Forensics & Evidence Handling (DFIR) Architecture
svg.desc: Digital Forensics diagram showing Memory Forensics (Volatility), Disk Forensics (Autopsy), Artifact Analysis (Windows Registry/Prefetch, Linux journald, CloudTrail), and Chain of Custody (NIST SP 800-86).
svg.text: Memory forensics, disk acquisition, OS artifact analysis, and NIST SP 800-86 Chain of Custody.
Live Volatile RAM & Static Storage Analysis
• Memory Forensics (Volatility / LiME): In-memory injection, process hollowing, network sockets
• Disk Acquisition (FTK Imager / dd): Bit-stream raw/E01 image creation with write-blockers
• Volatility Order: Capture volatile RAM prior to host shutdown or network isolation
• Windows Artifacts: Registry hives, Event Logs (Evtx), Prefetch, Shimcache, Amcache, USN Journal
• Linux Artifacts: Systemd journald, auth.log, bash history, auditd logs, cron jobs
• Cloud Artifacts: AWS CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GCP Audit Logs, Azure Activity Logs
CHAIN OF CUSTODY & EVIDENTIARY INTEGRITY (NIST SP 800-86)
Legal Evidence Integrity & Cryptographic Hash Verification
• Cryptographic Hashing: Calculate SHA-256 / SHA-512 hashes immediately upon evidence acquisition
• Custody Logging: Record acquiring investigator, date/time, physical/cloud location, & hash validation
• Read-Only Analysis: Always perform forensic timeline analysis on working copies; preserve master original
DFIR LIFECYCLE: LIVE RAM ACQUISITION → DISK BIT-STREAM IMAGE → ARTIFACT TIMELINE → CHAIN OF CUSTODY VERIFICATION
